title: FedCP: Separating Feature Information for Personalized Federated Learning via Conditional Policy

problem.claim: Personalized federated learning addresses privacy protection, collaborative learning, and statistical heterogeneity among clients.

gap.claim: Existing personalized federated learning methods mostly exploit global and personalized information in client-level model parameters while neglecting data as the source of both kinds of information.

contributions.claim: FedCP generates a conditional policy for each sample to separate global and personalized information in features and processes them with global and personalized heads, respectively.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments in computer vision and natural language processing show that FedCP outperforms eleven state-of-the-art methods by up to 6.69%.
FedCP reportedly maintains its superiority when some clients accidentally drop out.

narrative_sequence.summary: Personalized federated learning is motivated by privacy protection, collaborative learning, and client statistical heterogeneity.
Existing methods focus on client-level model parameters and neglect the data source of global and personalized information.
FedCP uses sample-specific conditional policies to separate feature information and route it through global and personalized heads.
The method is described as more fine-grained because personalization is handled at the sample level.
The authors report gains across computer vision and natural language processing and robustness to client dropouts.

unknowns: Datasets, evaluation metrics, and experimental settings are not specified.
The eleven comparison methods and the conditions producing the 6.69% improvement are not identified.
The dropout experiment protocol and quantitative results are not specified.
The conditional-policy architecture and training procedure are not described.
